comparator.academicYear: Current curriculum for the Fall 2026 cohort; checked 2026-09-29
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines one complete 180-EC Medicine pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 1 combines four patient-centred organ-system themes, a 6-EC observation and care placement, clinical and scientific methodology, academic formation and professional development. Year 2 deepens the same themes and longitudinal formation while preserving 18 EC of genuine elective space. Year 3 continues the themes and formation, includes a 12-EC medical bachelor thesis and culminates in a 14-EC preparation-for-practice block focused on clinical reasoning, history-taking and physical examination before clerkships. The official overview confirms the normalized identity, three-year 180-EC load, Dutch language, Amsterdam UMC location and RIO code 56551. Elective space is preserved without invented content. Review on 2026-10-17 reconfirmed the same current official curriculum: all settled components, EC, 18-EC elective space and absence of a formal route are preserved. Target-specific programme-interest registry rows support inclusive and sustainable healthcare as interests associated with this programme.
components: Patient-centred theme covering pregnancy, birth, and physical and sexual development.
Patient-centred theme covering the nervous system, eye and ear, and musculoskeletal system.
Patient-centred theme covering metabolic, hormonal and immunological regulation.
Patient-centred theme covering cardiovascular, pulmonary and renal systems.
Clinical epidemiology, statistics and evidence-based medicine.
Academic skills, scientific skills and humanities portfolio work.
Patient-centred study of autoimmune disease and endocrine and digestive-system disorders.
Patient-centred study of arrhythmia, coagulation disorders, pulmonary embolism and renal failure.
Genuine choice space consisting of fixed 12-week pathways or an approved individually assembled pathway, including possible study abroad.
Patient-centred study of complex orthopaedics, central functional disorders and psychiatric disorders.
Human development from embryo through older age, with population health, the older patient and the health-care system.
Final bachelor block preparing for medical clerkships, centred on clinical reasoning and assessment of physical examination and history-taking skills.

Patient-centred clinical care, diagnostic reasoning and professional medical skills
Scientific foundations, methods, data and evidence in medicine
Development, brain function, cognition and psychological experience of illness
Ethical and social questions in inclusive healthcare

Health behaviour, cognitive function and patients social experience

How do cognition, behaviour and social circumstances shape illness experience?

candidates.label: Health behaviour, cognition and patient experience in social context

alternatives.label: Biomedical disease mechanisms, health & research
alternatives.labelReason: Life, health, cognition and psychology courses form the substantive curriculum, supported by research methods, data analysis, ethics and mandatory PPD. The title describes biomedical and psychological study of health and disease without implying Medicine or clinical competence.
alternatives.concept: Study human health and disease through cellular biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, genetics, immunity, pharmacology, laboratory methods, epidemiology and psychological influences on illness. Research design, statistics, data handling and evidence synthesis support scientific investigation. This is a biomedical and health-science response to Medicine; supervised clinical reasoning, practical medical skills and patient care remain absent.
progression: Biomedical and brain/behaviour gateways precede all dependent courses. Cell biology, physiology, biochemistry and anatomy precede advanced pathology and pharmacology where feasible. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental statistics and the meta-analysis seminar. Formal prerequisites and exact planned availability pass. Data handling occurs before final-year evidence synthesis. Abnormal Psychology is placed before Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies as a useful advisory progression.

alternatives.label: Health, cognition, behaviour & social experience
alternatives.labelReason: Seventeen biomedical, cognition and psychology courses form the main curriculum. Sociology, qualitative inquiry, ethics, methods and public persuasion connect this substantial core to illness experience and social conditions. Inclusion is an application supported by these tools rather than a claim that all courses teach healthcare inclusion.
alternatives.concept: Study illness and health behaviour through physiology, brain function, cognitive impairment, developmental and clinical psychology. Sociology and qualitative inquiry examine how institutions, inequality and meanings shape illness experience; ethical reasoning and public persuasion provide specific analytical tools for questions of inclusion and health messages. This is an academic health-science programme, without medical consultation, clinical examination or supervised patient treatment.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, molecular pathology, infection/immunity, mechanisms of disease and laboratory work give way to perception/action, language neuroscience, social psychology, sociology, qualitative inquiry and public persuasion. This changes the priority from molecular and organ-system disease research to cognitive, psychological and social processes in health and illness.
progression: Brain/behaviour and biomedical gateways precede dependent cognition, psychology and pharmacology. Social psychology precedes advanced health psychology; sociology precedes qualitative inquiry. Introductory research methods precede experimental statistics and evidence synthesis. Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions and advanced language neuroscience. All exact terms and formal prerequisites pass; persuasive communication follows social psychology and ethics, but prior rhetoric is advisory rather than a formal prerequisite.

selection.assessment: Two alternatives were included sequentially. The third candidate, environmental sustainability of healthcare (18094, supported by 18123), was assessed independently. UCR offers lifecycle analysis, resource recovery, renewable technology, environmental governance and sustainability communication, but no sustained healthcare-operations, healthcare-waste/materials or sustainable clinical-service sequence. Combining enough environmental courses with health courses would produce two adjacent strands without concrete healthcare-specific contributions from all 23 non-PPD courses. It therefore does not support a complete coherent third response. Clinical care, diagnostic reasoning and treatment remain explicitly unfilled core gaps; their presence does not invalidate the two related academic responses.

notes.text: UvA Medicine integrates organ-system science with patient placements, clinical reasoning, medical skills and professional development. These UCR programmes study biomedical disease mechanisms or health through cognition, behaviour and social experience. They do not reproduce the medical clinical sequence, supervised patient care or preparation for clerkships.
